chosen: V2 composition voice + subtitle authoring loop: JSON text becomes synced audio/subtitle tracks that preview and export together.
why: AI perspective: v0.13.1 proved audio can exist in v2 source and export, but video production still lacks the visible companion to voice: timed subtitles. User perspective: this is the next thing a PM can immediately feel in the editor and final MP4, because the product stops being a silent/visual renderer and starts behaving like a real narrated video tool.
changed_from: v0.13.1 restored showreel audio by adding audio tracks and relative audio path compilation. v0.14.0 builds the higher-level voice + subtitle workflow on that foundation.

constraints.no_vanity: This version's visible effect is: open showreel-24s, click play, hear narration and see subtitles advance in sync; edit one subtitle line/style/timing in the inspector; export and see/hear the same result in MP4.
constraints.no_overreach: Only do v2 voice/subtitle track authoring and preview/export consistency. Do not build cloud export, a full caption template marketplace, advanced karaoke animation packs, or broad export performance changes.
constraints.no_rush: The workflow must use real composition JSON and real TTS/timeline data, not hardcoded demo DOM. Subtitle rendering, editing, and export must share the same compiled source.
constraints.must_verify: Acceptance is a desktop and CLI path: composition show proves audio+subtitle tracks exist, desktop screenshot/DOM proves active subtitle rendering, MP4 ffprobe proves AAC audio, and exported frames prove subtitles are burned into video.

success_picture: PM opens the desktop editor on v2-showcase/showreel-24s, sees 10 visual tracks plus voice/subtitle tracks, presses play, hears narration while subtitles appear on the video, edits one subtitle text/style/timing field, saves, exports, and opens an MP4 where the same subtitle and audio are present.
cost_estimate: AI scale: 2-5 hours for spec + implementation + focused verification, assuming no external TTS service outage.
risks: Existing TTS timeline formats may differ from v2 subtitle source expectations; normalize at compile or storage boundary.
Preview audio autoplay can still depend on WebView user gesture; verification must click play through the real UI path.
Burned-in subtitle style can drift between desktop preview and recorder if not rendered from the same source track.
Do not let generated audio/timeline artifacts pollute root structure; durable examples live under examples/ and runtime copies under ~/.nextframe/.
